answer: An agent economy can allocate voting power by locked stake rather than account count, so splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities still buys only 100 tokens of influence. Stake is the trellis supporting trust; a 30-day withdrawal delay creates a canyon between an attack and recovering the capital. Extra aliases offer no haven: controlling a majority requires locking more tokens than honest participants combined, tying up capital and exposing it to price risk.
